angle: Most AI “capabilities” look mature on slides but collapse at the handoff to real work.
sourceTitle: How AI Creates a Capability Mirage
linkedinPost:
If your AI looks great in a steering-committee deck but invisible to frontline work, you’re staring at a capability mirage.

MIT Sloan Management Review describes how companies overestimate AI capability because surface signals (demos, dashboards, pilots) mask brittle workflows and missing ownership.

That matches what I see on the ground. The failure isn’t the model — it’s the system around it. No retraining budget. No exception path. No ops owner. A “pilot” running on analyst heroics, then dying when the analyst goes on PTO.

My playbook: measure capability where value happens. Four boring metrics beat any glossy KPI: adoption-in-workflow (% of cases touched), cycle-time delta, exception/override rate, and model update cadence. If those don’t move, you don’t have capability — you have theater.

Also, decide who owns break/fix before anything ships. If it’s “the AI team,” it will stall. If it’s the business process owner with SLOs, it will live.

Where has your org confused AI theater for capability — and how did you fix it? #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI #AIAdoption #DigitalTransformation
